## How they got there
Arsenal finished as runners-up in the 2025-26 season after losing the Champions League final to Paris Saint-Germain on penalties. Their performance was defined by an exceptional profile during the league phase, highlighted by a Points per game value of 3.0 which beat 100% of teams in that first phase. This dominance extended to Goal difference per game at 2.38, also beating 100% of teams, and a defensive record of Opponent shots on target per game at 2.8, which was better than 97% of their peers.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model would have selected Arsenal, ranking them second inside its top two predictions for this season. With a probability of 24.6% to reach the final, the system viewed them as more likely to succeed than the base rate of 8.3%. The stage on that scale nearest to the model's expectation was semi-finals, reflecting an anticipated deep run. While Goal difference per game at 2.38 pushed the prediction up most with a SHAP contribution of 0.78, the model noted Attacks per game at 50.1 as the first stat pushing the prediction down most, with a negative contribution of -0.16.

## Weak spots
Fouls committed per game had a value of 13.9 and beat only 11% of that season's teams. Long passes (% of passes) recorded at 11.4 beat just 36% of that season's teams. Passes per game stood at 450, beating only 39% of that season's teams.

'Teams beaten (%)' figures say how many teams the club did better than on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where doing better means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Use 'significant' or 'significantly' only for a Holm-adjusted p-value comparison, never for other differences. Write plain markdown without tables.
